0.name: Genesis
0.description: Create an owned object and mark it solved. Pure Sui style: TxContext, no signer.
0.instructions:
# Level 0: Genesis

Your first Sui mission: create an object (it gets transferred to you), then call solve on it to flip the solved flag. All with TxContext—no signer in sight.

## Objectives

1. Call create to mint your Genesis object
2. Call solve with that object to set solved = true

1.name: Lockbox
1.description: Unlock the lockbox and drain it. The contract is a little too generous with secrets.
1.instructions:
# Level 1: Lockbox

The lockbox holds a password and a balance. Your mission: unlock it and drain the balance to zero. Sometimes the best way in is to see what the contract is willing to tell you.

## Objectives

- Unlock the lockbox
- Drain the balance to zero

2.name: Fallout
2.description: The contract thinks a certain address is the owner. Time to become that address.
2.instructions:
# Level 2: Fallout

A fallout-style contract: a vault with a get_owner function that was never properly implemented. Your job: figure out who the contract thinks the owner is, then withdraw and drain the vault.

## Objectives

- Drain the vault (balance = 0)

3.name: Blank Check
3.description: The contract doesn't ask pesky questions about the amount. Use that to your advantage.
3.instructions:
# Level 3: Blank Check

This one will let you "transfer" without checking the amount. Your mission: get your balance to zero and receive the Solved object. Sometimes the move nobody thought to forbid is the one that wins.

## Objectives

- Reduce your balance to zero and get the Solved object

4.name: Open Door
4.description: A flag unlocks the prize. The door check was forgotten.
4.instructions:
# Level 4: Open Door

Open Door: there's a flag that unlocks the Solved object. It was supposed to be admin-only, but the contract never checks who's calling. Your mission: set the flag and claim Solved.

## Objectives

- Set the flag and claim the Solved object

5.name: Double Entry
5.description: The ledger has two numbers that should stay in sync. They don't.
5.instructions:
# Level 5: Double Entry

Double Entry: the ledger keeps a total and your balance. They're supposed to match. Your mission: withdraw in a way that leaves total at zero but your balance still positive. When the books don't add up, that's your opening.

## Objectives

- Get total == 0 and my_balance > 0

6.name: Truncation
6.description: Fee math and integer division: make the numbers work in your favor.
6.instructions:
# Level 6: Truncation

Truncation: a fee pool with integer division and rounding. Your mission: deposit and withdraw so that fee_accumulated hits zero while total_deposits is still positive, then grab Solved. When math truncates, someone wins.

## Objectives

- Leave fee_accumulated == 0 and total_deposits > 0, then get Solved

7.name: Split Ledger
7.description: Registry and Wallet should agree. One of them didn't get the memo.
7.instructions:
# Level 7: Split Ledger

Split Ledger: a Registry and a Wallet that are supposed to stay consistent. Your mission: get the registry count to zero while your wallet balance is at least 200. Two books, one reality—make them disagree in your favor.

## Objectives

- Achieve registry.count == 0 and wallet.balance >= 200

8.name: Jackpot
8.description: The claim condition sounds right on paper. The numbers say otherwise.
8.instructions:
# Level 8: Jackpot

Jackpot: the "rewards" pool has a condition that seems fair until you do the math. Your mission: deposit a small amount and claim until the contract gives you the Solved object. Sometimes the fine print works for you.

## Objectives

- Get the Solved object by claiming rewards

9.name: Permit
9.description: The treasury accepts a permit. It doesn't bother marking it used.
9.instructions:
# Level 9: Permit

Permit: a treasury that spends via a "permit"—and never marks that permit as used. Your mission: use the permit to drain the treasury and claim Solved. One permit, one (or more?) shot. The contract isn't keeping score.

## Objectives

- Drain the treasury (balance = 0) and claim Solved

10.name: Queue
10.description: Empty the queue and trigger the solved condition. Work with the size limit.
10.instructions:
# Level 10: Queue

Queue: a max-size queue and a process function that rewards you when the queue is empty. Your mission: enqueue, process, repeat until the queue is empty and you get the Solved object.

## Objectives

- Get the Solved object by processing until the queue is empty

11.name: Price Feed
11.description: The pool trusts a single price. You can change who sets it.
11.instructions:
# Level 11: Price Feed

Price Feed: a pool that uses one price and lets someone update it. Your mission: set the price to your advantage, then swap so the reserves hit zero and the pool marks itself solved.

## Objectives

- Drain reserves so pool.solved = true

12.name: Master Key
12.description: The vault is locked behind an AdminCap. The cap can change hands.
12.instructions:
# Level 12: Master Key

Master Key: a vault locked behind an AdminCap—and that cap is transferable. Your mission: get the cap (maybe someone transfers it to you?), unlock the vault, and drain it for the Solved object. With great capability comes great opportunity.

## Objectives

- Drain the vault (balance = 0) and get Solved

13.name: Wrapper
13.description: A balance wrapper; the order of updates is wrong.
13.instructions:
# Level 13: Wrapper

The Wrapper lets you deposit and withdraw. The bug is in when the balance is updated versus when you "get" the funds. Your mission: drain the wrapper to zero and get the Solved object. Think about what happens if you withdraw twice in one transaction.

## Objectives

- Drain the wrapper (balance = 0) and get Solved

14.name: Ticket Stub
14.description: Deposit gives you a ticket stub; withdraw is supposed to consume it. Does it?
14.instructions:
# Level 14: Ticket Stub

Ticket Stub: deposit locks funds and gives you a stub (Receipt). Withdraw is supposed to consume that stub and credit the vault. Your mission: get the vault balance back to 1000 or more and claim the Solved object. If the stub isn't actually consumed, one stub might go a long way.

## Objectives

- Get vault.balance >= 1000 and claim Solved

15.name: Hot Pointer
15.description: Reference vs value: pointer reassignment corrupts the wrong field. Inspired by Lombard Finance.
15.instructions:
# Level 15: Hot Pointer

Hot Pointer: a treasury with limit and left. The code does a "reset" by reassigning a reference: \`left = limit\`. In Move that reassigns the pointer, not the value—so the next \`mint\` decrements \`limit\` instead of \`left\`. Your mission: create a treasury, then call \`reset_and_mint\` once with amount 1000 to corrupt \`limit\` and get the Solved object.

## Objectives

- Get the Solved object by triggering the pointer-reassignment bug

16.name: Wrong Pool
16.description: Withdraw takes a pool and a pool_id but never checks they match. Inspired by Navi Protocol.
16.instructions:
# Level 16: Wrong Pool

Wrong Pool: the contract has a vault pool (balance 1000) and you can create your own pool (balance 0). \`withdraw(pool, claimed_pool_id, amount)\` drains \`pool\` but doesn't validate that \`pool\`'s id matches \`claimed_pool_id\`. Your mission: drain the vault by calling withdraw with the vault pool and any pool_id, then get the Solved object.

## Objectives

- Drain the vault pool (balance = 0) and get Solved

17.name: Open Gate
17.description: An internal helper is marked public so anyone can set the solved flag. Inspired by Aftermath.
17.instructions:
# Level 17: Open Gate

Open Gate: a vault with a \`solved\` flag. \`set_solved_flag\` was meant to be internal (\`public(package)\`) but is \`public\`, so anyone can call it. Your mission: create a vault, call \`set_solved_flag\` on it, then \`claim_solved\` to get the Solved object.

## Objectives

- Set the flag and claim the Solved object

18.name: Wrong Repay
18.description: The receipt stores which pool was borrowed from, but repay never checks. Inspired by Cetus.
18.instructions:
# Level 18: Wrong Repay

Wrong Repay: create a "victim" pool (1000) and an "attacker" pool (0). \`borrow(pool, amount)\` gives you a Receipt that stores \`pool_id\`. \`repay(pool, receipt)\` credits \`pool\` with the receipt's amount but never asserts \`pool\` matches the receipt's \`pool_id\`. Your mission: borrow from the victim pool, repay using your attacker pool (wrong pool), then claim Solved when your pool reaches 1000.

## Objectives

- Get your pool's balance >= 1000 and claim Solved
